title: Ninus
summary: Ninus is dated in Raleigh's chronological table (1617), column Assyria, by a yeere of the World. No tier 1–4 chronology dates this person.
description: Added from the Raleigh import (The History of the World, 1617). Raleigh is display-only. He gives a yeere of the World, not a BC year, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year. Raleigh is display-only and is not converted to BC.

death.date: after a reign of two and fifty years, died A. M. 2017
death.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 164 (facsimile PDF p. 260)
death.note: The reign length, fifty-two years, is printed. A start year is not printed in this sentence. Page 171 places the beginning at A. M. 1957. The two statements are both entered and not reconciled. See open question K4.

reign.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 782b
reign.note: Year cell "2649 1967 310". The third printed figure 310 is the column "Floud", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 52 at the end of the name is the reign length he prints. The end year is not printed on this row. Column: Assyria.

reign.date: A. M. 1957, the year in which I have placed the beginning of Ninus’s reign
reign.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 171 (facsimile PDF p. 267)
reign.note: Reached by counting one thousand three hundred years back from the death of Sardanapalus at A. M. 3257. Not reconciled with the death at A. M. 2017 after fifty-two years. See open question K4.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 91; Castor, ap. Eusebius
reign.note: Not linked to Nimrod. See H3.

reign.date: “the complete sum of the years amounts to 1280”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 92; Castor, ap. Eusebius
reign.note: The sentence begins at the foot of p. 91: Castor's series runs from Ninus to a later Ninus after Sardanapallus. The numeral 1280 is on p. 92. The individual reigns of that canon are not printed in this edition (the text turns to Damascius). The 1280 is not Ninus's own reign.

reign.date: “from Ninus thirty generations, and more than 1,400 years”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 83; Diodorus Siculus, book 2
reign.note: The Assyrian empire. Not Ninus's personal 52 years from Castor.

reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 190; Velleius Paterculus, Roman History, book 1, chapter 6
reign.note: The Asiatic empire. Not a personal reign of Ninus or of Sardanapalus.

reign.date: “the thirty-third in succession from Ninus and Semiramis”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 190; Velleius Paterculus, Roman History, book 1, chapter 6
reign.note: Sardanapalus. semiramis-i was not used. The fragment does not say Semiramis I.

reign.date: “there has elapsed a period of 1,995 years”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 191; Velleius Paterculus, Roman History, book 1, chapter 6, and Aemilius Sura
reign.note: The words on p. 191. The sentence begins at the foot of p. 190: from the beginning of the reign of Ninus, who first obtained the empire. Aemilius Sura is named in the extract.
